newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Philip Morris sees Australian price war.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris sees Australian price war.

text.p: Philip Morris Inc's Australian unit chief executive Henry Goldberg said he expected a price war to erupt in Australia by June that would cost the sector A$100 million in earnings in calendar 1997.

Goldberg said in an interview published in The Australian newspaper on Wednesday that the pain would be shared by Philip Morris, Rothmans Australia Ltd and W.D. & H.O. Wills Holdings Ltd. He blamed Wills for starting the war.
"I don't believe Wills is going to make a profit this year," Goldberg said.
"Since (Wills chief executive Stuart) Watterton has taken over at Wills, the price discounting has been beyond reason, and Rothmans has joined in as well," he said.
A spokesman for Wills, which is about 67 percent owned by B.A.T. Industries, was not immediately available for comment.
Wills reported a A$13.27 million profit in calendar 1996, up from a loss of A$5.16 million in 1995, which was due to a price war two years ago. Wills is due to hold its annual meeting on Thursday.
Rothmans reported a net profit for the six months to September 30 of A$52.06 million, up from a A$110,000 profit in the corresponding half a year earlier, which was hit by the 1995 price war.
But Rothmans warned in November of deep discounting in some sectors of the market and said this provided some concern for the second half of the year.
Rothmans is 50 percent owned by Rothmans International Ltd, which is in turn 60 percent owned by Swiss-based Richemont AG and 40 percent by South African group Rembrandt Group Ltd.
A Rothmans spokesman was not immediately available for comment.
